review.summary: Phase 24's release-readiness chunk is genuinely qualified on the reviewed source a13067c6. I verified the recorded check snapshot (SHA256 4a0f765d) rather than its prose: all 73 commands exit 0, every record carries source_unchanged=true, and every executed_at falls in one contiguous 2026-10-19T23:07–23:33 window immediately after the live run at 23:05 — no stale or unexecuted evidence, and the single Python skip is an explicitly historical 0.1.1 dependency-freeze test out of 492 tests. The release gate is extended to the actual selected version: scripts/check-access-release.py:30 registers (24, '0.2.3'), and its phase-24 path binds both schema-3 clean package receipts to the current fingerprint, proves releaseCommit a5e1a74 is an ancestor of HEAD with an identical source fingerprint (bookkeeping excluded), re-reads every packaged input against both the filesystem and the release commit, and requires the retained archive to live inside that commit's own worktree (tools/release_delivery.py:158-172, closing attempt-1 finding 4). Old-consumer compatibility is real, not asserted: tools/management_consumers.py:66 forces the three 0.2.2 example sources and the native probe main.rs to byte-equal published bytes, and scripts/check-management-package.py:97-139 requires those exact bytes to compile and run from the extracted archive plus a separate consumer crate on both 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 (374s/357s receipts). Fresh service qualification is bounded and honestly scoped: the schema-2 receipt records one verified method (OAuth 200) and four 403 target-list probes with no mutations, the gate rejects anything else (tools/red_team_management.py:766-793 now requires the 4-item limitation set naming both the exercised api.sase profile and the unexercised api.apps default, closing attempt-1 finding 3), live_evidence.py pins crateVersion 0.2.3 and runtimeInputsSha256 to current source, and qualification.json reports liveVerified 1 / liveNotVerified 447. Changelog and docs match the plan's required disclosures exactly (DRAFT/ACTIVE narrowing, all five affected legacy status values, profiling_status migration, unchanged-wire/upstream-rejection caveat, Unknown(JsonValue)→Variant5/Variant3 transitions, typed projections out of extensions), and docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md is bound to the receipt by tools/test_live_acceptance_docs.py (closing attempt-1 finding 1). Runtime claims spot-check clean: targets.rs:26-46 carries the required rustdoc on both filters, :84-91 validates profiling_status pre-dispatch, :350 validates before paging and clones params per page, and generated.rs:8926-9009 implements typed-over-extension precedence with Patch omission/null/value and [REDACTED] Debug. I found no blocker or high issue; three low items remain (an access_policies execution-binding asymmetry introduced by skipping verify_offline_delivery for phase 24, pre-publication dead receipt links, and stale default CLI release identity).

findings.description: For 0.2.3 the readiness guard skips scripts/check-access-release.py:107-108 verify_offline_delivery, which for 0.2.1/0.2.2 explicitly required the archive to execute `run --example access_policies --all-features` and bound accessPolicyConsumerSourceSha256. The schema-3 wrapper's `required` list and its archive_command_executed/externalExampleConsumers assertions cover only test/check/doc commands plus response_defaults, red_team_dataplane, response_compatibility and red_team_management. scripts/check-package.py:169-170 and :191-206 still run the access-policy example and its external consumer, and any failure would fail the receipt, so no current evidence is weaker; but a future change that silently stopped executing that packaged consumer would no longer be rejected by the phase-24 gate.
findings.required_fix: Add `examples/access_policies.rs` to the verifier's required archive-example executions (or re-assert accessPolicyConsumerSourceSha256 and its consumer checkIndex) in scripts/check-management-package.py:verify_receipt so the 0.2.2-era binding strength is retained for 0.2.3.

findings.description: The 0.2.3 entry links docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.3.json and docs/checks/release-tag-v0.2.3.json, which do not exist yet; README.md:41-42 (packaged into the published crate) points the same two receipts at absolute git.cdot.io URLs, and docs/RELEASE.md:5-6 and docs/STABILITY.md:4 repeat the pattern. The surrounding prose is explicit that a missing receipt means publication is unverified, and tools/test_ci.py:346-350 deliberately defers receipt assertions until the workspace version matches the last publication, so this is presentation only: the published README will carry links that 404 until the post-publication bookkeeping commit lands on main.
findings.required_fix: Either render the unpublished 0.2.3 receipt references as plain paths until the receipts exist, or add the links in the post-publication bookkeeping commit, so no packaged document ships a dead reference.

findings.description: Module defaults still name the historical release (VERSION = '0.2.2', PHASE = 20) and are used as the CLI defaults at :239-240, while the active candidate is 0.2.3/phase 24 and docs/RELEASE.md:41 instructs invoking `--phase 24 --version 0.2.3`. A bare invocation checks the wrong release identity; it cannot fabricate acceptance (verify() line 194 and verify_source_commits() line 122 require the current source fingerprint, which the 0.2.2 commit no longer matches, so it fails), but the failure surfaces as a confusing source mismatch rather than a wrong-release error.
findings.required_fix: Make --phase/--version required, or default them to the active release identity, so the no-argument path cannot target a superseded release pair.

limitations: Read-only review: I executed nothing. All pass/fail conclusions rest on the recorded snapshot, receipts and ledgers plus source reading; I verified internal consistency, timestamps, source fingerprints and checkpoint bindings rather than reproducing any command.

Live acceptance for this source is one OAuth token exchange. The four profiling filter probes returned 403, so neither filter acceptance nor filtering effectiveness is established, and the shipped default profile https://api.apps.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-red-teaming/mgmt-plane was never exercised by this receipt — the probed profile was api.sase .../ai-red-teaming/mgmt. Vertex AI, N8N, client_session, audio and realtime provider workflows remain live-unverified. All of this is disclosed in the receipt, LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md and CHANGELOG.md.

I did not read any credential or tenant-registration file. The private-material receipt reports three repository files containing a pre-existing tenant identifier, all unchanged in HEAD and outside packaged source; I accepted that previously reviewed classification without independent inspection.

Publication, registry byte verification, the remote annotated tag and terminal remote CI are explicitly outside this chunk and remain unperformed. Readiness guards (scripts/check-prepublication.py, scripts/verify-publication.py:56-98, tools/release_delivery.py) were reviewed as code and unit-test coverage only; none of their online paths has executed.

Generated-model correctness was assessed through the compiler/clippy receipts, the independent fixture and oracle tests, and selected declarations (basic auth, Vertex, client_session, redact view). I did not audit the 6.7 MB generated.rs or the 2.1 MB schema graph exhaustively.

The phase-24 gate ran with --resume (docs/checks/phase-24-partial.json). I confirmed every record is on the same source fingerprint inside one 26-minute window and that final receipt checks carry checkpoint_bindings, but I did not verify the resume logic beyond its recorded output and tests.
Historical phases 1–23 and their immutable receipts were not re-audited; I judged only phase 24 readiness criteria and the cumulative regressions relevant to this scope.
